source.author: verg
source.text: Dicuntur geminae pestes cognomine Dirae, quas et Tartaream Nox intempesta Megaeram uno eodemque tulit partu paribusque revinxit serpentum spiris ventosasque addidit alas.
source.text_original: Dicuntur geminae pestes cognomine Dirae, / quas et Tartaream Nox intempesta Megaeram / uno eodemque tulit partu paribusque revinxit / serpentum spiris ventosasque addidit alas.
source.text_english: There are said to be twin plagues called the Dirae, whom untimely Night also bore, Tartarean Megaera, in one and the same birth, and bound them with coils of serpents like theirs, and added wings to them for the winds.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nec timet Ancaeum genetrix committere ponto, plena tulit quem rege maris.
reuse.text_original: nec timet Ancaeum genetrix committere ponto, / plena tulit quem rege maris.
reuse.text_english: nor does his mother fear to entrust Ancaeus to the sea, she who had borne him, full, by the sea-king.
